mainTopic: Shed and dangling wool of a בכור; the end of פרק הלוקח בהמה; how long an owner cares for a בכור, and why gifts to a כהן must not look like wages
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: would an owner delay offering an עולה in order to collect its wool, the way חכמים worry he would with a בכור? A ברייתא about plucking wool from a בכור תם is brought as proof, but the proof is rejected. The word 'plucks' was used only to show how far עקביא's leniency goes, while the משנה says 'shed' to show how far חכמים's strictness goes. The גמרא then defines dangling wool that 'does not appear with the fleece.' ריש לקיש and רב נתן בר אושעיא give two tests, and רבי אילעא explains that ריש לקיש chose the narrow test because every fleece has some dangling strands. The פרק הלוקח בהמה ends, and פרק עד כמה begins with a משנה about how long an owner must care for a בכור before giving it to the כהן, and about eating a בכור within its year. The גמרא derives the 30 and 50 days from the verses, through רב כהנא's pairing and then רבא's reading of 'תעשה', and leaves the exact number to the חכמים. It then explains why the owner may not hand over the בכור early: it looks like the כהן is earning his gift. A ברייתא forbids paying helpers with holy gifts, and explains why חכמים did not fine the owners who did so.

steps.title: Would an owner delay offering an עולה to collect its wool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides of its question about an עולה. Its main purpose is not כפרה, which suggests the owner might delay it. But it does atone for a missed עשה, which suggests he would not delay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since its main purpose is not to bring atonement, perhaps he will keep it around longer. Or perhaps, since an עולה also atones for a missed positive commandment, he will not keep it around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question about whether the worry of 'he will delay the animal' applies to an עולה. It gives two possible sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בכור, חכמים forbid shed wool because the owner might delay the animal to gather more wool. An עולה is not mainly brought for כפרה, so maybe there is no rush and the same worry applies. But an עולה does atone for neglecting a מצות עשה, so maybe the owner wants to bring it quickly and there is nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Atonement
He will keep it around / delay offering it
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
For a positive commandment (that was not done)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is saying an עולה has no כפרה at all. The point is only that כפרה is not its main purpose, unlike a חטאת. The question is how much urgency the owner feels.

phrases.aramaic: דְּעִיקַּר לָאו לְכַפָּרָה אָתֵי — מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: since its main purpose is not for atonement, he will keep it (delay it),
phrases.notes: First side: there is no urgency, so the worry exists.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעוֹלָה נָמֵי מְכַפְּרָא אַעֲשֵׂה —
phrases.english: or perhaps, since an עולה also atones for a positive commandment,
he will not keep it (delay it)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעוֹלָה נָמֵי מְכַפְּרָא אַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question that began on the previous amud
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the worry of delaying the animal (which is why shed wool of a בכור is forbidden) also apply to an עולה?

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא about plucking wool from a בכור תם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that wool plucked from an unblemished בכור stays forbidden, even after the animal gets a blemish and is slaughtered. The גמרא reads this to mean wool that fell out by itself is permitted. If that is true for a בכור, it is all the more true for an עולה, which people do not delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn, it is forbidden even though the animal later got a blemish and he slaughtered it. The reason is that he plucked it. But if it was torn out on its own, it is permitted. All the more so an עולה, which people do not delay, should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It reads the ברייתא as permitting wool that came out on its own, and applies this to an עולה with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא specifically says 'one who plucks.' The גמרא reads this precisely: only plucking is forbidden, and wool that falls out by itself is allowed. If even a בכור's fallen wool is allowed, then an עולה's fallen wool should certainly be allowed, since the worry of delay is weaker there.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
One who plucks (pulls out by hand)
An unblemished firstborn animal
It was torn out (on its own)
All the more so

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם,
phrases.english: even though a blemish later developed in it,
and he slaughtered it, the wool is forbidden.
The reason is because he plucked it; but if it was torn out on its own, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads the wording 'plucks' precisely.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן עוֹלָה דְּלָא מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ!
phrases.english: and all the more so an עולה, which one does not delay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 1
steps.raayaObject: That fallen wool of an עולה is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about plucking wool from a בכור תם, read precisely, plus a קל וחומר

steps.title: Fallen wool is also forbidden; 'plucks' shows עקביא's strength
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the precise reading. Wool torn out on its own from a בכור תם is forbidden too. The ברייתא said 'plucks' only to show that עקביא permits a blemished animal's wool even when it was plucked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same law applies even if it was torn out on its own: that is also forbidden. The ברייתא says 'plucks' to teach you how far עקביא goes, since for a blemished animal he permits even plucked wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. It explains that the word 'plucks' in the ברייתא was chosen for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's later section is about a בעל מום, where עקביא permits the wool even if it was plucked. To keep the wording the same, the earlier section also says 'plucks.' So the word 'plucks' does not hint that fallen wool is allowed, and the proof for עולה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
To show you the strength (how far an opinion goes)
עקביא בן מהללאל, the lenient opinion in this משנה
A blemished animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'plucks' as limiting the law to plucking. The ברייתא uses that word to match its next section about עקביא. It is not meant to exclude wool that falls out by itself.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ נִתְלַשׁ נָמֵי אָסוּר,
phrases.english: the same law applies: even if it was torn out on its own, it is also forbidden,
and the reason it teaches 'plucks'
is to show you the strength of עקביא's view,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְבַעַל מוּם אֲפִילּוּ בְּתוֹלֵשׁ נָמֵי שָׁרֵי.
phrases.english: that for a blemished animal, even when one plucks, it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ נִתְלַשׁ נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The precise reading of 'plucks', and so the קל וחומר to עולה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Plucks' was written to show the strength of עקביא's view, not to exclude wool that fell out on its own

steps.title: But the משנה says 'shed', not 'plucked'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this explanation. In the משנה, the dispute with עקביא is about wool that was shed, not wool that was plucked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn 'shed' in the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 3. The משנה's dispute between עקביא and חכמים is about wool that was shed, not plucked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case of עקביא's dispute is about plucking, why does the משנה describe it as shedding? The two sources seem to describe the dispute differently.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)?
Was shed / fell out

phrases.english: But didn't we learn 'shed' in the משנה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא presents עקביא's case as plucking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה describes the same dispute as shed wool, so the two sources seem to conflict

steps.title: Each source shows the strength of a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'shed' to show how far חכמים go: they forbid even shed wool. The ברייתא says 'plucks' to show how far עקביא goes: he permits even plucked wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught 'shed' to show you the strength of the Rabbis' view. The ברייתא taught 'plucks' to show you the strength of עקביא's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two sources picked different wordings on purpose, and each one highlights a different side of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'shed' shows that חכמים forbid the wool even in the mildest case. Saying 'plucks' shows that עקביא permits it even in the harshest case. So the sources do not conflict, and the explanation from step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught (the source chose this wording)
The strength of the Rabbis' (חכמים's) view

steps.whatToRemember: The proof about עולה from the word 'plucks' was rejected. 'Plucks' in the ברייתא shows how far עקביא's leniency goes. 'Shed' in the משנה shows how far חכמים's strictness goes. The question about עולה is still not answered here.

phrases.english: It (the משנה) taught 'shed' to show you the strength of the Rabbis' view,
it (the ברייתא) taught 'plucks' to show you the strength of עקביא's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seem to describe עקביא's dispute differently
steps.terutzMaskana: Each wording deliberately highlights the full reach of one side, so the explanation from step 3 holds

steps.title: What counts as wool that does not look like part of the fleece?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about dangling wool and asks how to define wool that 'does not appear with the fleece.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה spoke about dangling wool. What exactly is the case of wool that 'does not appear with the fleece'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about dangling wool and asks for a clear definition. This sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said dangling wool is permitted if it looks like part of the fleece and forbidden if it does not. 'Does not look like part of the fleece' is vague, so the גמרא wants a clear test for which strands are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Dangling wool: strands that are loose but have not fully fallen out
What is the case? A request to define a situation exactly
The fleece, meaning the wool that is shorn off

phrases.english: Dangling wool, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. It marks a new topic in the sugya.

phrases.english: What is the case of
'it does not appear with the fleece'?
phrases.notes: The words of the משנה being defined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה, after the עולה and בכור wool discussion ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear test for which dangling strands count as not part of the fleece.

steps.title: Two definitions of wool that is not part of the fleece
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says it is a strand whose root is turned upward. רב נתן בר אושעיא says it is a strand that does not press down together with the fleece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of ריש לקיש: any strand whose root is flipped so it faces the top. רב נתן בר אושעיא said: any strand that does not flatten down together with the rest of the fleece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to its question. Each answer is a different test for which strands are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's test is narrow: only a strand turned upside down, root facing out, is forbidden. רב נתן בר אושעיא's test is broader: any strand that sticks up when you press the fleece is forbidden. His test seems closer to the plain words 'does not appear with the fleece.'

keyTerms.meaning: Its root, the base end of the strand
Flipped toward the top, so the root faces outward
Gets pressed down or flattened together

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Reish Lakish said:
Any strand whose root is turned toward its top.
phrases.notes: The strand is upside down, with its root facing out.

phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya said:
Any strand that does not get pressed down with the fleece.
phrases.notes: When the fleece is pressed flat, this strand still sticks up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question with two different opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש: a strand with its root turned upward. רב נתן בר אושעיא: a strand that does not press down with the fleece.

steps.title: Why did ריש לקיש not accept the simpler definition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש did not define it like רב נתן בר אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש: what is his reason that he did not say like רב נתן בר אושעיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש chose a narrow, unusual test when רב נתן בר אושעיא's test fits the משנה's words better. This sets up רבי אילעא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Does not appear with the fleece' sounds like 'sticks out from the fleece,' which is רב נתן בר אושעיא's test. So ריש לקיש needs a reason for moving away from the plain meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא?
phrases.english: that he did not say like Rav Natan bar Oshaya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind ריש לקיש's opinion from the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ריש לקיש rejected the more natural definition.

steps.title: Every fleece has some dangling strands
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא explains that every fleece has some strands that stick out. Under the broader test, almost every fleece would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: ריש לקיש holds this way because it is impossible to have a fleece without some dangling strands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא answers the question. He explains why ריש לקיש could not accept the broader test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every fleece has some strands that stick up. If all of them were forbidden, the fleece of a dead בכור could almost never be used, and the משנה's permission would mean nothing. So ריש לקיש limits the forbidden strands to the clearly unusual ones that are turned upside down.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his view
Strands or hairs
It is impossible

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש takes the narrow test, root turned upward, because a test that forbids every strand sticking out would forbid nearly every fleece.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
Reish Lakish holds,
that since it is impossible for a fleece to exist
without dangling strands.
phrases.notes: So the broader test would forbid almost every fleece.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: קָסָבַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why ריש לקיש did not use רב נתן בר אושעיא's test.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every fleece has dangling strands, so the broader test would forbid almost all fleece. Therefore ריש לקיש uses a narrower test.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing הלוקח בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק called הלוקח בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הלוקח בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here. This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the discussion of this פרק is finished and a new פרק is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing words said when finishing a פרק
The name of the פרק that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who buys an animal.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.

steps.title: How long the owner must care for a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that the owner cares for a בכור 30 days for a small animal and 50 days for a large one. רבי יוסי says three months for a small animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For how long must a Jew take care of a בכור before giving it to the כהן? For a small animal, 30 days. For a large animal, 50 days. רבי יוסי says: for a small animal, three months.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It sets how long the owner must raise a firstborn animal before handing it to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner does not hand the בכור over at birth. He must first raise it for a set time. The תנא קמא gives 30 days for sheep and goats and 50 days for cattle. רבי יוסי disagrees only about small animals and gives them three months.

keyTerms.meaning: To take care of, to tend and raise
A small animal, such as a sheep or goat
A large animal, such as cattle
The משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA: Until how long
phrases.notes: The opening words of the new פרק, which is called עד כמה.

phrases.english: are Israelites obligated to take care of a firstborn?
For a small animal, thirty days,
and for a large animal, fifty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בַּדַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: for a small animal, three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיבִין לִיטַּפֵּל בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner raises a בכור for 30 days (small animal) or 50 days (large animal) before giving it to the כהן. רבי יוסי says three months for a small animal.

steps.title: When the owner may give the בכור to the כהן early
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן asks for the בכור early, the owner should not give it. But if the animal is blemished and the כהן wants to eat it, or it is unblemished in the time of the מקדש and he wants to offer it, the owner may give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן says during that time, 'Give it to me,' the owner should not give it to him. But if it has a מום and the כהן says, 'Give it to me so I can eat it,' it is allowed. And when the מקדש stands, if the animal is unblemished and the כהן says, 'Give it to me so I can offer it,' it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains what happens if the כהן asks for the בכור before the caring period is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the owner should not hand it over early, even if the כהן asks. There are two exceptions. A blemished בכור can be eaten right away, and an unblemished one can be offered right away when the מקדש stands. In both cases the כהן wants it for its proper use now, so early giving is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the time, meaning before the caring period ends
An animal with a blemish, which can be eaten as regular meat and not offered
Unblemished, fit to be offered on the מזבח
In the time when the בית המקדש stands

steps.confusionAlert: 'He should not give it' does not mean the כהן has no right to the בכור. It belongs to the כהן. The only question is timing: the owner keeps caring for it until the set period ends, except in the two cases listed.

phrases.english: If the priest said to him within the period:

phrases.aramaic: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי״ — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: 'Give it to me,' he should not give it to him.
But if it is blemished,
and the priest said to him, 'Give it to me so I may eat it,' it is permitted.
And in the time of the Temple, if it was unblemished,
and he said to him, 'Give it to me and I will sacrifice it,' it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by ruling on early transfer during the caring period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner should not give the בכור early just because the כהן asks. He may give it early if it is blemished and the כהן wants to eat it, or unblemished in the time of the מקדש and the כהן wants to offer it.

steps.title: A firstborn animal is eaten within its year
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a בכור must be eaten within its first year, whether unblemished or blemished. The source is the verse 'שנה בשנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The firstborn animal is eaten year by year, whether it is unblemished or blemished. As the verse says: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it, year by year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and gives a new rule. A בכור must be eaten within its first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'שנה בשנה' teaches a time limit: the בכור should not be kept past its first year. This applies to a בכור תם, which is brought as a קרבן, and to a בכור בעל מום, which the כהן eats outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Year by year: eaten within its own year
Unblemished, fit to be a קרבן
Has a blemish, so it is eaten as ordinary meat by the כהן

phrases.english: The firstborn is eaten year by year,
whether unblemished or blemished,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about the timing of a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any בכור, תם or בעל מום, must be eaten within its first year.

steps.title: A firstborn that becomes blemished during its year
steps.stepSummary: If the בכור gets a blemish during its first year, the owner may keep it for the full twelve months. After that, he may keep it only thirty more days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it developed a blemish within its year, he may keep it for all twelve months. After twelve months, he may keep it only thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a special case: a בכור that becomes blemished partway through its year. It tells us how long the owner may hold on to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish does not force the owner to rush the בכור out right away. He may still use the rest of the year. If the blemish appears only after the twelve months have passed, he gets a short grace period of thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish developed on it
He is permitted to keep it
Thirty days

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור is eaten within its year. If it becomes blemished, the owner may keep it through the twelve months, plus at most thirty days after that.

phrases.english: If a blemish developed on it within its year —

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he may keep it all twelve months.
After twelve months —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: he may keep it only thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the year rule for a בכור that became blemished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור that becomes blemished may be kept through its twelve months. After that, it may be kept only thirty more days.

steps.title: Where do the 30 and 50 days come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. The owner cares for the בכור 30 days for a small animal and 50 for a large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the Torah source of the משנה's waiting periods. This question sets up רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave exact numbers, 30 days for small animals and 50 for large ones, without a source. The גמרא wants to know which verse produces these specific numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (asks for the source)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is about the 30-day and 50-day care periods from the start of the משנה (step 11). It is not about the 'שנה בשנה' rule just quoted, which already gave its own verse.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the source of the earlier 30/50-day rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for caring for a בכור 30 days (small animal) or 50 days (large animal).

steps.title: רב כהנא pairs the verses
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns from שמות 22:28–29. 'בכור בניך', which links to the 30 days of פדיון הבן, is paired with 'לצאנך'. 'מלאתך ודמעך', which links to ביכורים brought 50 days after פסח, is paired with 'לשורך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The verse says 'The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me' and 'So you shall do with your sheep.' And 'Your fullness and your outflow you shall not delay' and 'So you shall do with your ox.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers by matching parts of one verse with the animals named in the next verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn son is redeemed at 30 days, so a sheep, which is a small animal, waits 30 days. ביכורים start coming on שבועות, 50 days after פסח, so an ox, which is a large animal, waits 50 days. Each time period comes from the topic it is linked to.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
Your firstborn son, redeemed at 30 days
Your first fruits and your first produce, linked to ביכורים and שבועות
Sheep (small animal) / ox (large animal)

steps.whyThisMatters: This pairing is what the rest of the sugya argues over. Which time period goes with which animal?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: For the verse says:
'The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,'
'So you shall do with your sheep.'
phrases.notes: Sheep get 30 days, like a firstborn son.

phrases.english: 'Your fullness and your outflow you shall not delay,'
'So you shall do with your ox.'
phrases.notes: Oxen get 50 days, like ביכורים from שבועות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 30 days for צאן come from בכור בניך (פדיון הבן). The 50 days for שור come from מלאתך ודמעך (ביכורים at שבועות).

steps.title: Why not reverse the pairing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the 30 days go with the ox and the 50 days with the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רב כהנא's matching seems arbitrary. The pairs could just as easily be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both time periods and both animals appear in the verses. Nothing obvious forces a sheep to take 30 days rather than 50. So the challenge is: what makes רב כהנא's matching the right one?

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it (a challenge that the opposite reading works too)

phrases.english: I can reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's pairing.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's matching of 30 days to צאן and 50 days to שור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses do not clearly say which period goes with which animal, so the opposite pairing is equally possible.

steps.title: Match first with first, last with last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב כהנא by matching in order. 'מלאתך', which comes first in the first verse, goes with 'שורך', which comes first in the second verse. 'בכור בניך', which comes later, goes with 'צאנך', which comes later.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable to match the earlier with the earlier, and the later with the later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason for רב כהנא's pairing: line things up by their order in the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמות 22:28, 'מלאתך ודמעך' comes before 'בכור בניך'. In 22:29, 'שורך' comes before 'צאנך'. Matching by order gives שור 50 days and צאן 30 days, which is exactly what the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason
What comes earlier / what comes later

phrases.english: It stands to reason that the earlier goes with the earlier,
and the later goes with the later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning based on word order
steps.terutzMaskana: Matching by order supports רב כהנא: מלאתך goes with שורך (50 days), and בכור בניך goes with צאנך (30 days).

steps.title: On the contrary, match what sits closest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the order argument. It is just as logical to match each topic to the animal right next to it, and that would give the ox 30 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: the one next to it goes with the one next to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. A different logic, closeness, points the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בכור בניך' ends verse 28, and 'כן תעשה לשורך' comes right after it. By closeness, the ox would get the 30 days of the firstborn son, the reverse of the משנה. So the order argument does not settle the question, and רב כהנא's source is left in doubt for now.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
That which is adjacent to it

steps.whatToRemember: Order and closeness point in opposite directions, so רב כהנא's derivation is left unproven. The גמרא will need a new approach.
steps.confusionAlert: Closeness here means the words sitting right next to each other across the two verses: 'בכור בניך' is followed immediately by 'לשורך'. It does not mean which topics are similar.

phrases.english: On the contrary, what is adjacent goes with what is adjacent to it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the order-based defense.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the order-based reasoning, and with it the support for רב כהנא's pairing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Closeness is an equally strong rule, and it gives the reverse result (שור gets 30 days), so order cannot decide the question.

steps.title: רבא finds a new source in the word 'you shall do'
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops רב כהנא's matching approach. He learns from the word 'תעשה' that the ox gets an extra period of care beyond the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The verse says 'you shall do.' The Torah added for you another act of 'doing' for your ox.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the previous reading was just knocked down, רבא gives a brand-new source for why the ox is cared for longer than the sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' means the old derivation is dropped. רבא reads the word 'תעשה' as adding something extra for the ox. So the ox does not stop at the sheep's 30 days. It gets an additional period on top of that.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the previous answer and give a new one)
אמורא who gives the new derivation
'You shall do'. This is the word רבא builds on
An additional act of 'doing', meaning extra care

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ox gets exactly 30 days. He is saying the ox gets MORE than the sheep. The exact number comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse says "you shall do,"
the verse added for you
another act of doing for your ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's derivation, which was rejected in Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: New derivation replacing the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order-based matching could just as easily give the ox 30 days
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'תעשה' gives the ox an added period beyond the sheep's 30 days

steps.title: Why not sixty days for the ox?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: if the ox gets another 'doing', maybe it is another full 30 days, which makes 60.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the ox gets sixty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. If the ox gets an extra period, why not double the sheep's 30 days and make it 60?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's word 'תעשה' only says 'more'. It does not say how much more. The natural guess is a repeat of the same 30 days, which gives 60, not the 50 our משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (we could say instead)
Sixty

phrases.english: But say: sixty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's derivation because it does not pin down 50
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An additional 'doing' could be another 30 days, which totals 60 and not 50

steps.title: The Torah left the exact number to the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The verse only tells us the ox gets more. The exact amount was given to the חכמים, who set it at 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse handed this over only to the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the Torah does not give the exact number, and the חכמים decided it is 50 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse gives the idea: extra time for the ox. The חכמים fill in the detail of how much. So we do not need a verse that says 50 exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse did not hand you over (did not leave the matter)
The Sages

phrases.english: The verse did not hand you over
except to the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'sixty' challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra period must be a fixed 30 days, totaling 60
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse only sets 'extra'. The חכמים fixed the total at 50.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same derivation as רבא: 'תעשה' adds extra care for the ox, and the amount was left to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: 'Give Me the firstborn of your sons… so shall you do to your sheep.' I might think the same applies to your ox. That is why the verse says 'you shall do.' The Torah added another 'doing' for your ox, and handed it over only to the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said, as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first thinks the ox might have the same 30 days as the sheep, like a firstborn son. Then the word 'תעשה' teaches that the ox gets extra time, and the exact amount is up to the חכמים. This matches both רבא's answer and the reply to 'sixty'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (support from a ברייתא)
One might have thought
Therefore the verse says
Your sheep / small animals

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
"The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,"
"so shall you do to your sheep"
Might it be the same for your ox too?
The verse says: "you shall do"
the verse added for you
another act of doing for your ox,
and the verse handed it over only to the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's derivation and the answer to 'sixty'
steps.raayaObject: רבא's derivation from 'תעשה' together with the delegation to the חכמים

steps.title: The rule: 30 days for a small animal, 50 for a large one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states the practical rule that comes from this derivation. Small animals get 30 days of care and large animals get 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: How long must a Jew take care of a בכור? A small animal, 30 days. A large animal, 50 days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now states the final rule that the derivation produces, matching our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 30 days for a small animal come from the link to a firstborn son. The 50 days for a large animal are the number the חכמים set for the extra 'doing'. This is the same rule as the משנה we opened with.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said
To take care of / tend
Small animal (sheep, goat)
Large animal (cattle)

steps.whatToRemember: The owner takes care of a בכור for 30 days if it is a small animal and 50 days if it is a large animal. The extra time for the large animal comes from 'תעשה', and the number 50 was set by the חכמים.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Until when are Israelites obligated
to take care of a firstborn?
With a small animal, thirty days;
with a large one, fifty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the halacha that follows from the derivation in the ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Small animal: 30 days. Large animal: 50 days.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: three months for a small animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees about small animals. He says they need 3 months of care because raising them takes so much effort.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A small animal needs three months, because caring for it takes a lot of work.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion in the ברייתא disagrees about the small animal and says it must be cared for longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gave a small animal 30 days. רבי יוסי says it needs 3 months, because a young sheep or goat is hard to raise and is not ready to be handed over sooner.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who disagrees about small animals
Three months
Its care takes a lot of effort

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
With a small animal, three months,
because its care is extensive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion about the small animal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small animal must be cared for three months

steps.title: Why a small animal is hard to raise
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains רבי יוסי's reason. The small animal's teeth are thin, so it cannot eat most foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: because its teeth are thin.
steps.whatsHappening: A short teaching explains why caring for a small animal takes so much effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said the care is extensive. This line gives the reason: a young sheep's teeth are small and weak, so it cannot eat regular food and needs extra time to grow.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher taught (a short ברייתא)
Its teeth are thin / small

phrases.english: It was taught: because its teeth are thin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יוסי's 'its care is extensive'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small animal's care is extensive because its teeth are small

steps.title: If the כהן asks for the בכור early, do not give it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה and quotes its next line: if the כהן asks for the בכור during the care period, the owner should not give it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן says to him during the waiting time, 'Give it to me,' he should not give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the next line of the משנה (step 12) so it can explain it. During the care period, the owner may not hand the animal over even if the כהן asks for it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has finished explaining the source for the 30 and 50 days. It now turns to the משנה's next ruling: the owner may not shorten the care period even when the כהן himself wants the animal early. The גמרא will next ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the set time (the care period)
Give it to me
He should not give it to him

phrases.english: If the kohen said to him
within the time, "Give it to me,"
phrases.notes: Within the 30 or 50 days of care.

phrases.english: he should not give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ברייתא and quotes the next ruling of the משנה (step 12) so that it can be analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner may not give the בכור to the כהן before the care period ends, even if the כהן requests it.

steps.title: Why may he not give it early?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the owner can't hand over the animal if the כהן wants it. This sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן is happy to take it and care for it himself, there seems to be no harm done. The question is what problem the משנה is worried about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it is forbidden to give the בכור to the כהן early when he asks for it.

steps.title: It looks like a כהן working for his gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that it looks like a כהן who helps at the threshing floor in order to earn תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: because he looks like a כהן who helps out at the threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains the problem. If the כהן takes the animal early, he saves the owner the work of caring for it, so it looks like he is earning the בכור as payment for a favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתנות כהונה are supposed to be a free gift, not wages. When the כהן takes over the owner's burden, the gift looks like payment, much like a כהן who helps at the granary so that he will be given תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Looks like / appears as
Who helps / assists
The threshing floor, where grain is processed and תרומה is given

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that מתנות כהונה must never look like payment for work. This principle is spelled out in the next ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Because he appears
like a kohen who helps out at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: A כהן who helps so that he will be given תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking the בכור early makes it look like the כהן is earning the gift by sparing the owner work, like a כהן who helps at the granary.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids paying helpers with תרומה and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that כהנים, לויים and poor people who help out may not be paid with תרומה or מעשר. Doing so desecrates them, and two פסוקים speak against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: כהנים, לויים and poor people who help out at the shepherd's place, the threshing floor, or the slaughterhouse may not be given תרומה or מעשר as their wages. If people do this, they have desecrated it. About them the verse says, 'You have corrupted the covenant of לוי,' and it also says, 'Do not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, so that you do not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing the general rule behind רב ששת's comparison. Holy gifts may not be used to pay people for their help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only תרומה and מעשר as the forbidden wages. The three places are typical spots where helpers might hope to get gifts. Perhaps each place hints at a related gift, such as the בכור at the shepherd's place or זרוע לחיים וקיבה at the slaughterhouse, but the text does not say so. Turning these gifts into wages is called חילול, and two פסוקים are brought against it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
As their wages
They desecrated (the holy gift)
You have corrupted the covenant of Levi (מלאכי ב:ח)
And it says (introduces a second פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source rule that מתנות כהונה may not be used as payment. The rule about the בכור in step 27 is one application of it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The kohanim, the Levites, and the poor
who help out at the shepherds' place,
and at the threshing floors, and at the slaughterhouses —
we do not give them
terumah and maaser as their wages,
and if they do so, they have desecrated,
and about them the verse says:
"You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,"
and it says:
"And the holy things of the children of Israel
you shall not desecrate, so that you do not die."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם וְהָעֲנִיִּים הַמְסַיְּיעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source of the principle behind רב ששת's comparison to a כהן helping at the granary.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's concern that a gift must not look like payment for help.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding the payment of כהנים, לויים and poor people with תרומה and מעשר.

steps.title: Why bring a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to add 'and it says' with a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the second פסוק adds that the first one did not already teach. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק already condemns the practice. A second פסוק must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What does 'and it says' add?

phrases.english: What is "and it says" for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the ברייתא in step 30 is structured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק teaches beyond the first.

steps.title: The second verse teaches a death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק only shows that it is wrong. The second shows that it carries מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you were to say there is no death penalty, come and hear: 'Do not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, so that you do not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק is there to show the punishment is death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'You corrupted the covenant of Levi' alone, we might think it is a sin with no death penalty. The words 'and you shall not die' show that it is serious enough to bring מיתה בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
Death (here, a heavenly death penalty)
Come and hear

phrases.english: And if you would say: there is no death penalty —
come and hear:
"And the holy things of the children of Israel
you shall not desecrate, so that you do not die."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִיתָה לָא — תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק shows that the sin carries a death penalty, which the first פסוק alone would not show.

steps.title: The Sages wanted to fine the owners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the חכמים wanted to penalize owners who paid with תרומה by making them separate תרומה again from their own produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages wanted to penalize them, and to make them separate תרומה again on that produce, at their own full expense.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now tells us about a fine the חכמים considered for owners who paid helpers with holy gifts. This sets up the question of why the fine was never made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner saved money by paying wages with gifts he owed anyway. The proposed fine would make him give the gift a second time from his own produce, so that he would not gain from doing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: To penalize them (a rabbinic fine)
Separate (set aside a gift from produce)
From their own (at full cost), or complete

phrases.english: And the Sages wished to penalize them,
and to have them separate on their account
terumah from their own, in full,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of step 30 with a possible fine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים considered requiring owners to separate תרומה a second time as a penalty.

steps.title: Why did they not fine them?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the חכמים did not go ahead with the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they not penalize them?
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the חכמים wanted to fine the owners, the text asks why they held back. This sets up the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine seems fair, since the owner gained from a forbidden act. So there must be some danger in it.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason
They penalized them

phrases.english: And for what reason did they not penalize them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the fine of step 33 was not enacted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים decided against the fine.

steps.title: The fine could cause mistakes in separating terumah
steps.stepSummary: Making people separate again might make them think the produce was never properly tithed. They might then use already-exempt produce to separate for produce that still owes its gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they would come to separate from exempt produce for obligated produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the fine could lead to a halachic mistake, so the חכמים did not make it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדאורייתא, the first separation counted, so the produce is already פטור. If the חכמים required a second separation, people would think the first one did not work and treat the produce as still טבל. They might then separate from this פטור produce on behalf of other חיוב produce, and that separation does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / lest
Produce that is exempt (already tithed)
Produce that is still obligated (untithed)

steps.confusionAlert: The fine was not dropped because paying with תרומה is permitted. It is still forbidden and a חילול. The fine was dropped only because it might lead to mistakes in separating tithes.
steps.whatToRemember: Holy gifts may never be used as wages, and this is also why a כהן may not take a בכור early. The חכמים skipped a fine only to avoid confusion about which produce is already tithed.

phrases.english: Perhaps they would come to separate
from the exempt on behalf of the obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאַפְרוֹשֵׁי מִן הַפְּטוּר עַל הַחִיּוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second separation would make people treat already-exempt produce as untithed and use it to tithe for obligated produce.

steps.title: Opening a rule that covers all the cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts a new statement that applies to every case it has discussed. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in all of them, there is (in them)…
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up its next move: it begins a rule that applies to all the cases it already discussed. Only the opening words appear here, so the learner should wait for the next passage to see what the rule actually is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וּבְכוּלָּן ('and in all of them') signals a shift. The ברייתא is no longer discussing the fine it decided not to impose (Step 35). It is now stating something true of every case together. The phrase יֵשׁ בָּהֶן ('there is in them') announces that some law or problem applies across all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And in all of them. The word gathers every case mentioned so far into one group.
There is in them. This introduces a law or problem that applies to the cases.
All of them. A common גמרא word for summing up a list of cases.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a complete sentence. Do not try to figure out the rule from these three words alone. The content of 'there is in them…' comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And in all of them there is (in them)…
phrases.notes: An incomplete opening. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ברייתא's explanation of why the חכמים did not impose a fine. It begins a rule covering all the cases together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling is not yet stated. The ברייתא only announces that some law applies to all the cases, and the content follows on the next amud.
